title: Why AI has a weird attention span you must learn to manage · hancrafted
description: AI's attention span, its context window, is a limited resource you have to actively manage: one chat per job, a handoff after real progress or before a break, and for bigger projects one planner chat that hands each step to a fresh chat.

What's really in the window Nothing carries over by itself a model holds nothing between requests; memory across chats exists only when an application stores notes outside the model and puts them back into the context 1 . Sources (1) Han, Why does an LLM forget everything between chats? (earlier research file, excludes consumer chat apps) ( opens in a new tab ) github.com Documented for Claude Code its instructions and its saved notes are loaded at the start of every conversation, and Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, How Claude remembers your project ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Loading has a cost longer instruction files consume more context and reduce adherence, and only the first 200 lines or 25KB of the notes index load at the start 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, How Claude remembers your project ( opens in a new tab ) code.claude.com Chat apps document the effect Claude's app saves memory as topics so the next conversation already knows what changed 1 , and Gemini remembers information you share, even in new chats 2 ; that the apps load it at the start is an inference. Sources (2) Anthropic, Use Claude's chat search and memory to build on previous conversations ( opens in a new tab ) support.claude.com Google, Manage what Gemini remembers about you and customize responses ( opens in a new tab ) support.google.com Not every feature preloads Claude's past-chat search is fetched on request 1 , and ChatGPT looks for relevant context only when it is likely to improve a response 2 . Sources (2) Anthropic, Use Claude's chat search and memory to build on previous conversations ( opens in a new tab ) support.claude.com OpenAI, Memory in ChatGPT ( opens in a new tab ) help.openai.com

One innocent question Everything is loaded with basic web search every result is loaded into the context window, much of it irrelevant to the request 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Web search tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com It stays search results count as input tokens, in the turn itself and in later turns, and are passed back into later requests, so they remain part of the window 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Web search tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com A PDF is the big bite Anthropic estimates an average web page at about 2,500 tokens and a research-paper PDF at about 125,000 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Web fetch tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com The remedy vendors filter before the window or cap the returned tokens 1 ; OpenAI describes the same shape, with deep research tapping hundreds of sources 2 . Sources (2) Anthropic, Web fetch tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com OpenAI, Web search (API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) developers.openai.com API figures, not app figures these sources describe developer tools; how many pages a given chat app loads per question is not published 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Web search tool (Claude API documentation) ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com

You can't watch the meter Documented for Claude for users with code execution enabled, Claude summarises earlier messages when a conversation approaches the context limit 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, How do usage and length limits work? ( opens in a new tab ) support.claude.com The only sign the page describes you occasionally seeing Claude "organizing its thoughts", and announces no notice each time; that it hides this on purpose is an inference 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, How do usage and length limits work? ( opens in a new tab ) support.claude.com Full history is kept the whole chat is preserved so Claude can reference it after summarising 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, How do usage and length limits work? ( opens in a new tab ) support.claude.com A summary can lose things Anthropic warns that over-aggressive compaction can lose subtle but critical context whose importance only shows later 1 . Sources (1) Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents ( opens in a new tab ) anthropic.com Other apps are unknown no vendor page found documents summarising in ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot, and a chat interface may instead drop the oldest content first 1 ; OpenAI's compaction is documented for its API and is opaque 2 . Sources (2) Anthropic, Context windows ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com OpenAI, Compaction ( opens in a new tab ) developers.openai.com

The long phone call 0:00 – 0:33 A long chat is a long call Imagine the last long phone call you had with someone close, a sister, a friend, your mum. You called to settle one thing, and an hour later you hung up. Before I say a word about AI, I want you to feel what that call left you with, because the question I want to ask you is whether a long AI chat does the same thing to you, so the call comes first and the chat second.

The AI's attention span 0:00 – 0:17 Why it happens So far you have seen what happens. Now the cause, because once you know how the AI holds a chat, the pattern stops being a surprise, and only after that do we look at what it does to your answers.

What fills the window 0:00 – 0:13 More in there than you typed You have seen the window fill with your messages. But your messages are only a part of it, so the next question is what else goes in without you noticing.

What's really in the window 0:00 – 0:13 More than the chat What you see in the chat is only part of what the AI reads. The chat is the visible slice, and around it sit other parts that you never typed. 0:13 – 0:25 Starting instructions First, the starting instructions: text placed in front of your first message, before you type a single word. That way the AI is already briefed before you say anything. 0:25 – 0:43 Memory Second, memory: short notes about you, saved earlier and put back in front of the AI, which is why a new chat already knows a few things about you. It is useful, and it is one more thing in the window. 0:43 – 0:57 The rest The rest are attached files, web pages the AI read, and results from tools and connectors. I only name them today. What matters is that they all share the same window as your chat.

One innocent question 0:00 – 0:13 Three venues Say you ask: find three venues in Lisbon. It is a small question. The answer is three options in a few lines, and behind it the AI ran two searches. 0:13 – 0:24 What you don't see Those searches bring back extracts of web pages that you never see. Each one is a modest bite, and the window takes it and moves on. 0:24 – 0:45 The catering PDF Then you point at the catering offers in the project folder and ask which one fits. The answer is one line, Sabor Verde. To give it, the AI read the whole catering PDF, all twenty pages, and that one question filled the window far more than anything before it. 0:45 – 1:05 The intern Give an intern the same task and they would read the whole file first too, before telling you one line. The AI does exactly that, only fast, and it shows you just the result. There is nothing wrong with it, you only need to know it happened. 1:05 – 1:20 A big bite So one short question can take a big bite out of the window while the chat looks as small as before. Keep that in mind when a chat feels full sooner than you expected.

You can't watch the meter 0:00 – 0:13 Her own notes Your sister doesn't keep the call. She keeps her own notes of it, a few scribbled lines: Mum's phone, the renovation, Pepper and the cake. A few lines instead of everything. 0:13 – 0:27 The app does something like it The app does something like it. When a chat gets long, older messages can be squeezed into a short summary, so the conversation can go on instead of hitting the wall. 0:27 – 0:38 You can't watch the meter And here is the catch: the chat looks the same. Every bubble is still there, so you can't rely on a gauge, you rely on habits. 0:38 – 0:52 Why the budget survived Why did the budget survive here? Because you flagged the 12,300 over budget just before, so it was fresh when the summary was written, and the plan fits 40,000 euro again. That was timing.
Managing the attention span 0:00 – 0:09 You manage by habit You can't read a gauge, so you build habits. First the everyday ones, and then the one for a big project.
